video_title: Jalen Brunson Among All-Time Guards?! Roy Hibbert on Knicks BENCH as XFactor for Championship

quotes.speaker: Roy Hibbert
quotes.summary_phrase: Roy Hibbert on Victor Wembanyama not shaking hands with the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: I don't have a personal relationship with these guys, but you leave it out there on the court.
quotes.quote: One of the most well-respected players I feel like I played with is David West, who we revere as a vet. He actually, when we played the Heat and we lost either Game 6 or Game 7, the last time we were all together, Paul George, George Hill and myself, David West and I got up and left right after the end of the game. We didn't shake hands. To me, I always felt like we just went to war. I don't have a personal relationship with these guys, but you leave it out there on the court. We got a little bit of flak for that at the time. I can understand where people are coming from, but I'd be okay if they didn't shake hands, to be honest with you. Just keep it moving.

quotes.speaker: Roy Hibbert
quotes.summary_phrase: Roy Hibbert on Jalen Brunson's place among all-time Knicks greats
quotes.excerpt: I saw something about how Brunson is the greatest Knick. I feel like he's on the precipice.
quotes.quote: I saw something about how Brunson is the greatest Knick. I feel like he's on the precipice for that. For me, it's still Patrick Ewing, obviously a Georgetown great. But at the same time, this team, what a difference a year has made in terms of where they were last year. Tom Thibodeau as a coach is not going to kick somebody while they're down. Obviously, they brought somebody else new in and it was able to hit the ground running.

quotes.speaker: Roy Hibbert
quotes.summary_phrase: Roy Hibbert on the importance of the Knicks' bench production
quotes.excerpt: One of the biggest things to me was the fact that the Knicks used their bench.
quotes.quote: One of the biggest things to me was the fact that the Knicks used their bench. Josh Hart, he played throughout the series when there was foul trouble. Jordan Clarkson, who is more of a vet now, is able to come in and spell some minutes for some guys. Miles McBride, Immanuel Quickley had two points, 10 rebounds. I really felt that the use of the bench, even though they didn't have great numbers, was able to spell some time for those guys to be able to get out there and the starters to finish off the game strong.

quotes.speaker: Roy Hibbert
quotes.summary_phrase: Roy Hibbert on the Knicks' composure during their playoff run
quotes.excerpt: They were down by 13 in the third quarter. In my mind, I'm like, the Knicks have them.
quotes.quote: French Montana has a song, 'Don't Panic,' and I felt that's exactly what the Knicks did. They did not panic whatsoever. They were down by 13 in the third quarter. In my mind, I'm like, the Knicks have them exactly where they want them. They're just going to keep grinding you over and over and over. OG Anunoby didn't have the greatest scoring game, but at the same time, he was able to defend, rebound, he made some really good passes. So they didn't panic at all, and obviously, Brunson did the Brunson thing.

quotes.speaker: Roy Hibbert
quotes.summary_phrase: Roy Hibbert on Jalen Brunson's unique scoring ability as a guard
quotes.excerpt: He's a scoring guard. I feel like the days of the point guard getting the offense going are great.
quotes.quote: He's a scoring guard. I feel like the days of the point guard getting the offense going, distributing the ball, having 10 plus assists, which would be great, that's not what he does. He's brought in to be able to score. And just like how Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is a scoring guard, obviously he's bigger than Brunson, but to me, I never fell into that narrative like, oh, you have a small guard, he's not going to be able to finish.

quotes.speaker: Roy Hibbert
quotes.summary_phrase: Roy Hibbert on Trae Young's impact on winning compared to Brunson
quotes.excerpt: Trae Young is spectacular in terms of scoring, but he doesn't affect winning in a great way.
quotes.quote: I look at a different Trae Young. Trae Young is spectacular in terms of scoring, but he doesn't affect winning, I feel like, in a great way in terms of on both ends of the court. It's a little bit of fluff numbers right there. So I feel like every situation is a little bit different. If Trae Young was in this position right here, I feel like things might have been different. And I'm not trying to throw him under the bus, but I feel like that narrative of a small guard is not going to help you win goes out the window. You have to have the right small guard, and this dude has a tough mentality.

quotes.speaker: Roy Hibbert
quotes.summary_phrase: Roy Hibbert on Victor Wembanyama's physical development needs
quotes.excerpt: I don't want him to get bigger. I want him to get stronger.
quotes.quote: I like his attitude. I love that he can get away with the push to Brunson in the back of the head, yes. People are going to get away with things. They're going to play dirty, they want to win. But at the same time, I go back to what Boogie said a couple segments ago in terms of he doesn't want him to get bigger. He wants him to get stronger. I think that's great. My wife was watching the game with me and I was saying, a lot of people say once he puts on a little bit more weight, he's going to be able to hold his own. He's pretty much able to score outside, mid-range. What I like to see him get stronger, like Boogie said, maybe go to the block maybe once or twice.

quotes.speaker: Roy Hibbert
quotes.summary_phrase: Roy Hibbert on Wembanyama needing to play 'dirtier' in the paint
quotes.excerpt: I would like to see him get a little bit more of a little bit dirtier in the paint.
quotes.quote: I would like to see him get a little bit more of a little bit dirtier in the paint. Because you guys said before, a lot of contested shots, bad shots they were taking down the stretches of the game. I think the false sense of security of how easy they were able to score in the first three quarters of the game, it just didn't fit towards the end of the game. I would like to see him, you know, get a little bit more of a little bit dirtier in the paint. You catch that thing like how Dirk Nowitzki used to do around the free throw and turn face, observe, see the court, and then try to get to work because he's one two dribble and he's able to get to the rim.

quotes.speaker: Roy Hibbert
quotes.summary_phrase: Roy Hibbert on the evolution of modern NBA offenses
quotes.excerpt: I want to know what happened to the Spurs offense.
quotes.quote: I want to know what happened to the Spurs offense. I feel like when these guys were playing and myself, you play against the Spurs, you're going to get a back-door cut at some point. Manu Ginobili is going to slice you up. Tony Parker is going to do something. It was just so much of, I guess, modern basketball in terms of come down, pick and roll, and then try to score one-on-one. And I feel like the days of that San Antonio offense, that crisp offense, is just not there anymore. And I felt like the culture there, the coaching tree, I thought that you would see that at some points in time.

quotes.speaker: Roy Hibbert
quotes.summary_phrase: Roy Hibbert on how Gregg Popovich's role has changed the Spurs
quotes.excerpt: I also think the head man, that head seat change, changed a lot of that offense.
quotes.quote: I also think the head man, that head seat change, changed a lot of that offense. I mean, obviously Pops is not the head guy there anymore. I mean, he is there, but it's not the same. But when we think about that, you know, that legendary offense that they used to run, head man in charge changed, so I think a lot of that changes as well.
